source: Struware CS2024, Ver 2024-03-08 (www.struware.com) - a commercial wind-load program, an implementation of ASCE 7-16 written by a third party
report: Struware published example calculation set, 'Wind Loads - MWFRS h<=60' (Low-rise Buildings)', sheet 7 of 34
basis: Wind Loads : ASCE 7-16, IBC 2021. The edition is PRINTED ON THE SHEET, which is what closes the 7-10 vs 7-16 open item the handover raised.
status: complete - every input and every printed output is captured, the run is reproducible from this file alone
why_this_run: The published worked example already in the handover is ASCE 7-10 at theta = 26.57 deg. It pins the 20 and 30 degree rows of the Fig. 28.3-1 table but says nothing about the 0-5 degree row - which is the ONLY row a PEB ever uses (a 1:10 roof is 5.7 deg, a 0.5:12 roof is 2.4 deg). This run is at theta = 1.2 deg and prints the whole table, both load cases, both signs of internal pressure.

printed_outputs.note_on_a: least horizontal dimension 175 ft -> 0.1 x 175 = 17.5 ft; 0.4h = 0.4 x 62 = 24.8 ft; the SMALLER is 17.5. Floor 0.04 x 175 = 7.0 ft and 3 ft, neither binds. This exercises the 'smaller of' branch with 0.1B governing.
printed_outputs.note_on_zone_2_length: 87.5 ft = 175/2 - the zone 2/3 boundary sits at the ridge, i.e. mid-width.

ultimate_surface_pressures_psf.comment: columns are Case A (-GCpi, +GCpi) then Case B (-GCpi, +GCpi)

printed_outputs.minimum_load_note_printed_by_struware: The code requires the MWFRS be designed for a min ultimate force of 16 psf multiplied by the wall area plus an 8 psf force applied to the vertical projection of the roof.
printed_outputs.why_that_note_is_recorded: It is ASCE 7-16 Sect. 28.3.4, and this package does NOT apply it. Recorded here so the coverage gap declared in loads/wind.py has a citation behind it rather than a memory.

horizontal_mwfrs_simple_diaphragm_psf.comment: Struware's 'Horizontal MWFRS Simple Diaphragm Pressures', transverse direction. These are the NET across-the-frame pressures - windward zone minus leeward zone - in which the internal pressure cancels. They are exactly the quantity the Sect. 28.3.4 minimum is compared against.
horizontal_mwfrs_simple_diaphragm_psf.negative_control_for_the_minimum: 24.7 psf > 16 psf and |-11.5| psf > 8 psf, so Sect. 28.3.4 does NOT govern this building. A minimum-load check that reported 'governs' here would be wrong, and that is what makes this a control rather than only a confirmation.

flags_this_can_close: wind.gcpf_table - all 8 Load Case A values at theta <= 5 deg and all 12 Load Case B values, exact
wind.velocity_pressure - Kz 1.144 at 62 ft Exposure C, and qh 35.9 psf
wind.internal_pressure_sign - 20 zone/case pairs printed with BOTH signs of GCpi, so p = qh(GCpf - GCpi) is confirmed term by term and in the direction that governs uplift
wind.end_zone_width - the 'smaller of' branch, with 0.1B governing

wind.minimum_design_load - the four printed simple-diaphragm net pressures reproduce net_horizontal_pressures exactly, Struware prints the Sect. 28.3.4 rule text verbatim, and its building is a NEGATIVE control in which the minimum does not govern
flags_this_cannot_close: wind.angle_interpolation - this run is a single angle in the flat band, so it exercises no interpolation at all. Closed instead by the theta = 26.57 deg worked example.
what_this_run_does_NOT_cover: The 20, 30, 45 and 90 degree rows of Fig. 28.3-1 are not printed here. See the VERIFIED block in loads/wind.py for what each of those rows does rest on.
Torsional load cases, parapet and overhang pressures: Struware prints parapet numbers, this package does not compute them. Declared as coverage gaps.
